questions: Does the introductory three-factor account make the minimum sufficient for the selected trigger, or state only a necessary condition?

Could all three factors be cumulative requirements as a contextual completion? Their linked referents and the nonbusiness guidance motivate considering this alternative, but neither establishes conjunction as the complete trigger; replacing the explicit minimum would require further support.
Does the qualified regulatory-intent passage affect only business classification or also qualify trigger satisfaction independently?
Does “such services” incorporate regulated status into the business factor, and does “the business” make hong_kong entail or presuppose business? How should absent or unknown referents be classified?

What do the missing dependency and incorporated Circular and Ordinance establish about completeness and qualifications? Any parallel-language comparison would also require the same edition and experimental variant and an established basis for interpretive precedence.

The earlier selected-factor proposal is not retained: no supplied wording establishes a separate selection mechanism or factor-specific conditions. Is there additional source language supporting one beyond ordinary existential quantification?

Case-dependent input classifications and incorporated authority remain external to the encoded predicate.

This conditional interpretation treats the introductory account as complete for the selected antecedent, making the minimum sufficient. The source does not expressly establish that completeness.
All inputs concern the same office, services and business; no semantic independence or input truth values are assumed.

Applicable regulated-activity carve-outs have been resolved. Treating the remaining contextual qualifications as fully reflected in input classification is an additional, disputed assumption of this executable reading.

citations.quote: The issue of whether a single family office is required to be licensed under the Ordinance is determined by reference to three key factors, at least one of which must be present in order to give rise to a licensing obligation
secondly, the family office is carrying on a business in the provision of such services; and thirdly, the business is carried on in Hong Kong.

readings.distinction: The first interpretation reads the inclusive minimum as a sufficient selected trigger through a pragmatic completeness inference. The rival below retains the same connective but rejects that sufficiency inference. Executability does not resolve this disagreement.

readings.distinction: After considering both readings, this is preferred as the narrower textual inference because necessity is explicit and sufficiency is not. The contextual qualifications reinforce caution without settling the rival completeness inference. The available partial constraint is that trigger satisfaction implies at least one factor; it is not a total Boolean function for the requested antecedent.

vocabulary_concerns: The three supplied facts can express disjunction or conjunction, but neither their availability nor critic agreement establishes a sufficient legal trigger. The necessary-minimum reading supplies only a one-way constraint, which cannot be returned as the requested total antecedent predicate using these facts.

Shared-service and shared-business references require consistent classifications. Boolean storage does not establish independence; hong_kong=true with business=false may reflect inconsistent or presupposition-failing inputs. No default false value is justified when the relevant business is absent.
The source treats carrying on a business in Hong Kong as a case-dependent assessment. Splitting it into business and hong_kong requires an unverified classification convention.

The business input compresses occupation or duty, continuity, profit capability, profit purpose, income and operating-expense reimbursement, ordinary-course treatment and regulatory intent. These qualifications remain external and cannot become a mechanical profit test or unconditional family-office exemption.

The regulated input absorbs resolved carve-outs. The described carve-out concerns Type 9 services solely to specified related entities; it does not establish a blanket exclusion from all regulated activities.

Missing factual inputs and unresolved interpretive sufficiency are different uncertainties. Fully classified inputs may still leave trigger satisfaction unresolved under the necessary-minimum reading.

The fixed vocabulary cannot separately test whether regulatory intent or ordinary-course qualifications affect the trigger beyond business classification. Assuming that all such qualifications are absorbed into inputs remains disputed.
